headline: 3,500 daily limit: Saint Martin’s to reopen to tourists on Nov 1
summary: The coral island will be open for visitors from November 1 to March 15, 2027, with new environmental restrictions to protect biodiversity.
details: Tourism restrictions on Saint Martin’s Island, Bangladesh’s only coral island and an environmentally critical area, will be relaxed from November 1.
Visitors will be allowed to travel to the island until March 15, 2027, under specific environmental rules decided at an inter-ministerial meeting.
To protect the island's biodiversity, the average number of tourists visiting the island must not exceed 3,500 per day.
Each visitor will be required to pay a Tk 100 environmental conservation fee, which will be managed by the Department of Environment.
Authorized tourist vessels will continue to operate from the Nuniyachhara jetty in Cox’s Bazar.
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has mandated that no vessel can operate on the route without its prior approval.
All previously issued directives on environmental conservation will remain in force to ensure the island's ecological balance.
caption:
Planning a trip to the coral island? Saint Martin’s is reopening on November 1 with a 3,500 daily visitor limit.

Tourism restrictions on Saint Martin’s Island, Bangladesh’s only coral island and an environmentally critical area, will be relaxed from November 1.

Visitors will be allowed to travel to the island until March 15, 2027, under specific environmental rules decided at an inter-ministerial meeting.

To protect the island's biodiversity, the average number of tourists visiting the island must not exceed 3,500 per day.

Each visitor will be required to pay a Tk 100 environmental conservation fee, which will be managed by the Department of Environment.

Authorized tourist vessels will continue to operate from the Nuniyachhara jetty in Cox’s Bazar.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has mandated that no vessel can operate on the route without its prior approval.

All previously issued directives on environmental conservation will remain in force to ensure the island's ecological balance.
